name: FL-03
label: Likely R

key_factors: Strong Republican district with a -10 PVI
Incumbent Kat Cammack running with a large fundraising edge
Democratic challenger Seth Harp has raised only about $38,000
Prediction markets price Republican win at 94%
model.rationale: The fundamentals point firmly to Cammack: a -10 partisan lean, incumbency, and a roughly 50-to-1 fundraising advantage over Harp, with no polls or expert ratings suggesting vulnerability. Markets price this at 94% Republican, consistent with a double-digit expected margin.
model.watch: Any late polling showing the challenger within single digits, or significant outside spending against Cammack, would warrant moving the race toward the tossup range.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Kat Cammack seeks another term in a north-central Florida district that leans Republican by about ten points. She enters with roughly $2 million raised and $877,000 on hand, while Democratic nominee Seth Harp has raised under $40,000 with minimal cash remaining. An independent is also on the ballot but has shown little financial traction.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, and prediction markets give the Republican side about a 94% chance of winning. With the incumbent well-funded in a favorable seat and the challenger lacking resources, the race is expected to stay comfortably in Republican hands, though the absence of polling leaves some room for uncertainty.
